Chapter 6 — Navigating the Dip: Building Resilience and Endurance.
So, you’ve picked your hill and decided to go all in on mastery. Now comes the tough part—the dip. This is that long, sometimes discouraging stretch where progress crawls, setbacks pop up left and right, and it feels so tempting to just throw in the towel.
But here’s the thing—making it through the dip isn’t really about powering through with brute force. It’s about building resilience. It’s about having the mental and emotional tools to keep moving forward, even when the climb gets steep.
Think about resilience like a muscle. Nobody’s born with it maxed out. You build it, bit by bit, by facing challenges and not giving up. Every time you push through a tough spot, you get just a little stronger for the next one.
If you want to build up that resilience during the dip, here are a few things you can try:
First, break your journey into smaller milestones. Instead of staring up at the distant summit, focus on the next step right in front of you. Celebrate those small wins along the way—they’ll help you keep your momentum.
Next, try reframing setbacks as feedback. When things stall out, don’t see it as failure. Instead, ask yourself, “What can I learn from this?” Not, “Why am I not there yet?” That little shift in mindset can make all the difference.
Another important one—reach out to your support network. Talk to people you trust. Share what you’re struggling with. Sometimes, just knowing you’re not alone makes the dip feel a lot less intimidating.
And don’t forget to remind yourself of your “why.” Go back to those reasons you started this journey in the first place. That sense of purpose can give you the fuel you need when your motivation starts to fade.
Think about all the real-life stories you know—a writer who faced rejection after rejection before finally landing that breakthrough book, or a startup founder grinding through years of slow growth before things finally took off. In every case, the dip wasn’t a signal to quit. It was just a necessary part of getting to mastery.
Remember, being resilient isn’t about pretending the hard stuff doesn’t hurt, or acting like everything’s easy. It’s about facing the struggle, managing your energy, and just putting one foot in front of the other.
Over time, that steady persistence is what separates the folks who make it to the summit from the ones who turn back too soon.
